title: Stability field guide + play scripts (2026)
content:
Purpose
This is a compact field guide intended to help product, platform, and SRE teams run cross-functional reliability experiments, define measurable SLOs, and execute safe rollouts. It is a working doc: lightweight, opinionated, and oriented toward fast feedback cycles rather than exhaustive process.

High-level approach (one-sentence):
Define a small set of customer-impact signals, design short experiments (2–6 wks) to validate operational assumptions, and automate signal collection + escalation so teams can iterate with low cognitive overhead.

How to use this doc
- Quick reference for SLO templates, canary checklists, and communication scripts.
- Operating rhythm suggestions (weekly syncs, lightweight decision logs).
- Includes 4 "play scripts" (concise step sequences) you can copy into incident runbooks or PR descriptions.

Core definitions (shorthand we use here)
- User-visible error rate: percentage of requests that produce incorrect, failed, or missing output as perceived by caller code (500-level responses, empty outputs, or structured failures).
- Per-path p95 latency: 95th percentile end-to-end request latency for a specific API route + model.
- Availability SLO: uptime relative to an error budget window (typically 30d).
- Quality SLO: relative model-quality pass-rate on a curated prompt set.

SLO design checklist (fast pass)
1) Pick 2–3 signals max: broadly applicable (error rate, p95 latency, and quality).
2) Choose window: 7d for alpha experiments, 30d for team SLOs, 90d for org-level commitments.
3) Decide burn policy: continuous vs. burst-tolerant.
4) Measurement method: aggregate by customer token or by production route; prefer request-level attribution.
5) Alert thresholds: 30% of budget burned -> advisory; 60% -> mitigation planning; 100% -> mandatory rollback or traffic limit.

Minimum telemetry to collect
- Route, model version, region, instance-type, request tokens, response tokens, outcome classification (ok / degraded / failed), latency_ms
- Trace id, timestamp, sampled stack traces for <1% slow tails
- Canary-level labels for staging/traffic-split experiments

Play scripts (copyable)
1) Canary launch — conservative traffic ramp (for new model variant)
- Preconditions: baseline SLOs stable for 14 days, automated metrics pipeline for canary signals in place.
- Steps: 1) Create canary deployment + tag dataset; 2) Open canary dashboard (link template in linked_artifacts); 3) Start at 1% traffic, run 48h; 4) Evaluate error rate and p95 vs baseline using A/B test page; 5) If both signals <=2 sigma from baseline, 5% for 48h; 6) Repeat doubling cadence to 25% max; 7) At any exceedance of alert threshold, pause ramp and trigger mitigation play.
- Decision: product+SRE sign-off required at 25% if rollout continues.

2) Rapid mitigation (when error budget burn > 60% in 24h)
- Steps: 1) Post to #ops-urgent with subject "URGENT: rapid-mitigation <service> <slo>"; 2) Snapshot traffic split and model versions; 3) Shift 25% traffic to fallback model variant; 4) Open incident stub and assign owner; 5) Run quick triage (5–10m) to identify root surface (infra, model, data).
- Communication script: "Observed SLO burn >60% for <service>. We are shifting traffic and investigating. ETA 30m for update."

3) Quality regression experiment (model eval-driven)
- Purpose: validate that a model-change does not degrade tracked prompt-set quality.
- Steps: 1) Define eval set (50–200 prompts reflecting top customer flows); 2) Run automated eval harness comparing baseline vs candidate; 3) If pass-rate drop >1.5% absolute, promote to internal review; 4) Run small canary only for non-critical routes pending review.

4) Post-incident decomposition + learning capture
- Steps: 1) 24–72h after incident, owner runs a 60–90m blameless decomp with product, SRE, infra, and solutions engineers; 2) Fill short form: timeline (5 bullet), root cause (one sentence), the contributing factors (3 bullets), immediate fixes (2 bullets), durable mitigations (3 bullets); 3) Publish summary to #ops-weekly and link to incident page.

Sample lightweight SLO template (copy into PR or ticket)
- SLO name: <service>-availability-30d
- Target: 99.9%
- Window: 30d
- Measurement: route-level user-visible error rate (exclude internal health-checks)
- Alerting thresholds: advisory at 30% budget, action at 60% budget
- Owner: <team-owner> (pager: @person)
- Rationale: supports main customer flow; outage risk leads to direct revenue impact.

Decision log format (one line per decision — to keep small)
- Date | Decision | Owner | Context link | Rollback plan
- Example: 2026-01-20 | Defaulting to quantized-8bit runtime for chat-small models in us-west-2 | Maya Chen | jira:SRE-4123 | Rollback: move to float16 worker pool

Communication templates (email / slack)
- Incident initial post: "Heads up: seeing elevated error rate for <route>. We are switching traffic and investigating. Next update in 30m. Owner: @<owner>"
- Canary OK: "Canary at 5% for <variant> shows no material change in error or latency after 48h. Recommend continue ramp."

Operational experiments backlog (starter list)
- A: Measure impact of continuous batching at low-traffic tails on p95 latency (2 wk experiment). Owner: Priya Nair. Ticket: PLAT-3789.
- B: Prefix-KV cache invalidation strategy (compare TTL 5m vs 30m) for burst-heavy routes (4 wk). Owner: Liam Rivera.
- C: Quality alerting pilot: automatic regression detection on production prompts (evaluate false positive rate). Owner: Ethan Gomez.

Meeting cadence recommendation (minimal)
- Weekly 30m sync: operational signals review + 1 blocker deep-dive (invite: product reliability rep, infra lead, SRE owner).
- Monthly 60m: experiment review + decision log updates (wider stakeholders).

Ownership matrix (text table you can paste into PR)
- SLO definition: product + SRE
- Measurement infra: platform metrics team
- Alerting/Oncall: SRE rotations
- Canary rollout execution: solutions eng + infra

Low-friction artifacts to create for each experiment
- A dedicated dashboard link (single page with 6 widgets),
- A two-line incident stub (template),
- A 1-paragraph rollout rationale pinned to the PR,
- A JIRA ticket using the label "slo-experiment".

Risk register (short)
- Model regressions: mitigations = canary + eval harness + automatic rollback rule.
- Metric correctness: mitigations = sampling + daily sanity checks and small test harness.
- Too many SLOs: mitigations = limit to 3 per service; retire spurious ones quarterly.

Open questions / TODOs (working)
- What is the canonical owner for cross-model quality SLOs? (product vs applied-ml)
- Quick audit of existing dashboards: are we missing route-level p95 by model? (ownership: metrics infra)
- Draft a short training for product PMs on SLO basics (target: 2x 30m sessions).

Appendix: quick links and templates
- Incident stub template: https://confluence.company/reliability/incident-stub-template
- Canary dashboard template: confluence:REL-FIELDGUIDE-001
- Experiment JIRA template: JIRA:SRE-4123

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally compact. If a team wants a deeper playbook we should convert a subset of these plays into a richer runbook with runbook steps and automation hooks. The goal here is to lower the barrier for cross-team experiments and reduce long synchronous review loops.

Revision history
- 2026-01-12 Maya Chen: first draft, core plays and templates
- 2026-01-20 Priya Nair: added canary cadence detail and experiment backlog
- 2026-02-03 Liam Rivera: clarified telemetry minimums and decision log format
